fact: The Ministry of Information, Communication Technology and Postal Services reported on 4 September 2025 that its leadership estimated a budget for the operations of the Access to Information Commission, which it calls a parastatal facing operating challenges; the amount was not given and the budget is estimated, not voted.

The FY 2024/25 budget performance report lists the Access for Information Commission among the Public Administration agencies whose allocations are reported against IFMIS actuals; the report prints no date, so its published date is used.

The Minister of Information's 6 September 2023 conference paper lists the Information Commission (IC) as one of six parastatals under the Ministry of Information, Communication Technology and Postal Services.

fact: South Sudan's UNESCO SDG 16.10.2 return describes an access to information legal guarantee that provides for a national Information Commission with oversight, appeals, monitoring, enforcement and mediation roles.
The return says the Information Commission is 'under establishment', with no online request tool, no annual report and no statistics on requests or appeals in 2023.
Advocate Johnson Juma says South Sudan's Access to Information Act, enacted in 2013, gives every citizen the right to access official information and records of government.
The Union of Journalists of South Sudan's secretary general says the Access to Information Act is one of three media laws in place, though not fully implemented.

Standard Zone News reports that South Sudan has an Access to Information Act of 2013 giving every citizen the right to information held by public bodies, and that journalists report public institutions ignoring requests despite it.
